findings.title: Scalar flow_lift_factor is inverted: lifting water hotter RAISES COP (up to 2.02x), breaking batch parity
findings.claim: ThermalModel.flow_lift_factor returns max(0.25, carnot_ref/carnot_flow), which is >1 for every flow above the 35 degC reference, so compute_cop (valve plant, direct-plant curve) and compute_cop_dhw rise with flow/tank temperature on every climate, while the batch twin _batch_cop applies carnot_flow/carnot_ref.

findings.title: temperature_from_c is not the inverse of normalize_temperature_c: every Fahrenheit set-point write is wrong
findings.claim: inputs.temperature_from_c(c, unit) multiplies by the unit's to-Celsius factor instead of dividing by it, so for the three Fahrenheit spellings a value written and read back through normalize_temperature_c is not the value written: 21.5 degC is written as 43.94 degF (6.6 degC) instead of 70.7 degF.

findings.title: tariff._exact_topk_sum sums the k smallest excesses: the scalar capacity charge and its batch twin disagree
findings.claim: tariff._exact_topk_sum returns sum(sort(excess)[:k]), the k smallest values, where its docstring and its batch twin (`np.sort(x, axis=1)[:, -k:]`) take the k largest; for every k above 1 with more than k windows the scalar _plateau_aware_topk_sum differs from _plateau_aware_topk_sum_batch (4 of 12 probes), peak_cost_smooth from peak_cost_batch (1 of 4), and the solve's scalar objective from objective_batch under a per-window capacity tariff (2 of 8, relative difference 1.4).
findings.mechanism: The rule `the billed top-k` is written twice: once as tariff._exact_topk_sum (tariff.py:916), which the exact published charge peak_cost (tariff.py:1038) and the solver's scalar term _plateau_aware_topk_sum (tariff.py:958) call, and once inline in _plateau_aware_topk_sum_batch (tariff.py:943), which the batched objective calls for the finite-difference gradient. The scalar copy slices the wrong end of the sort. With [1, 5, 3, 4, 2, 0.5] and k = 2 the scalar returns 1.5 and the twin 9.0. It bites whenever more than k excesses are compared with k above 1: `Peaks on different days` off (peak_tariff_distinct_days False, the per-window rule the option's own text names), or a horizon spanning more plan days than peak_count. There the published projected_peak_cost bills the smallest excesses (often 0), and the solver's line search reads a capacity term its gradient was not taken from. findings.title: German run-optimization refusal names {entry_id}; production passes {entry_ids}, so the de message cannot render
findings.claim: translations/de.json exceptions.run_optimization_no_prices.message uses placeholder {entry_id} while strings.json, sv.json and both raise sites pass only entry_ids, so 1 of 3 shipped languages cannot format the message the optimize_now button raises.
findings.mechanism: button.py ForceOptimizationButton.async_press (and services.py run_optimization) raise HomeAssistantError(translation_key='run_optimization_no_prices', translation_placeholders={'entry_ids': ...}); the de string formats {entry_id}. str.format raises KeyError; Home Assistant's translation loader validates a localized string's placeholders against the English one and discards a mismatching one, so German users get the English text (plus a load-time error log) instead of German.
